cds.text: Investigate how interpersonal language choices vary with context and the roles people take on
Understand that cooperation relies on shared social conventions, including turn-taking language, which vary with formality
Explore language used to build relationships in formal and informal situations
Explore language for appreciating texts and giving reasons for preferences
Understand how evaluative and emotive language, such as modal verbs, can be varied to be more or less forceful
Identify subjective language of opinion and feeling, and objective language of factual reporting
Use interaction skills to engage with topics, receive and give instructions, extend ideas, and express and respond to opinions
Use interaction skills to contribute to conversations and discussions, sharing information and ideas
Listen for key points to carry out tasks and contribute to discussions, acknowledging other opinions, linking responses to the topic, and extending ideas
Create, rehearse and deliver short presentations for familiar audiences, using purpose-appropriate structure, topic vocabulary, and varied tone, volume and pace
Plan, rehearse and deliver short presentations to inform, express opinions or tell stories, with clear structure, elaborated details, precise vocabulary, visual features and suitable delivery
Plan, rehearse and deliver structured presentations to report, tell stories, recount events or argue, using subjective and objective language, complex sentences and visual features
